reasoning_traces.think:
Homography estimation maps source image pixels to destination pixels via a 3x3 projective transformation matrix. It relies on identifying invariant feature points across views. Failure occurs when viewpoint differences exceed 60 degrees yaw or 45 degrees pitch, leading to vanishing points outside the image frame. Low-texture regions cause insufficient feature correspondences, while severe illumination shifts break descriptor matching. Robustness is achieved through multi-scale analysis (SIFT) and outlier rejection (RANSAC), which filter false positives introduced by repetitive patterns or noise.
